bullets.title: LITE: Optical components sold out through early 2029; AI demand far exceeds supply
bullets.body: Lumentum CEO confirmed the company is completely sold out of optical components for AI servers through early 2029, extending the prior sell-out timeline by ~6 months. The company cannot meet ~70% of 2027 demand for some products. LITE up ~6-7% pre-market; sympathetic moves in AAOI, COHR, CIEN, FN, GLW.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone 18 Pro/Max builds cut 15-20% on weak demand and price-hike pushback
bullets.body: Nikkei reported Apple told suppliers to cut iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max component orders by at least 15% in October; Mizuho buyside checks confirm 15-20% cuts. The iPhone Duo launching Oct 23 at $1,999 is also expected to see weak demand. AAPL down ~2.3% pre-market; SWKS (~60% AAPL revenue) and QRVO (~50%) flagged at risk.

bullets.title: T/VZ/TMUS: SpaceX $8B 800MHz spectrum buy sparks massive selloff; towers rally
bullets.body: SpaceX acquired ~13.5-14 MHz of 800MHz low-band spectrum from Grain Management for ~$8B (~$1.70/MHz-PoP), moving toward wireless carrier status and threatening T/VZ/TMUS. T down 6-10%, VZ down 5-10%, TMUS down 7.5-12% with heavy put-heavy options volume (T: 112k contracts 210% above avg; VZ: 99k contracts 239% above avg). Citi's Rollins sees 21% upside for CCI, 20% for SBAC, 10% for AMT; maintains Buy on all three tower names.

bullets.title: NFLX: ~5% workforce RIF expected before earnings; stock implications mixed
bullets.body: Puck News and multiple broker notes flag Netflix is preparing to lay off approximately 5% of its workforce as part of a restructuring, with announcement expected before Q3 earnings. No guidance revision flagged yet. Wolfe's 3Q preview separately notes Netflix top-10 viewing fell -11% y/y (vs -9% prior quarter) though showing sequential stabilization vs. Q2's -13%.

bullets.title: BKNG/EXPE/ABNB: Agentic AI (Meta Muse, Google) threatening OTA commission pools; stocks -15-25%
bullets.body: Meta's Muse and Instinct AI agents now complete full travel bookings without OTA integration using browser automation and one-time cards; Google launched hotel booking in AI Mode in late August. OTA stocks down 15-25% YTD on this threat. Wolfe survey: only 27% of consumers tried Muse and 64% won't trust agents with credit cards, suggesting near-term risk is better-than-feared. Expedia leads AI-readiness scorecard; Airbnb sits at bottom. Muse could generate $30-50B M/LT revenue opportunity for META itself.

bullets.title: NVDA: AWS capex bullish, Trainium sold out; supply chain tight on memory rationing
bullets.body: AWS CEO Garman signaled no capex slowdown; AWS Trainium is sold out through late 2027 with GPU fulfillment running only ~60%. NVDA is rationing memory by reducing memory specs on GPUs to maximize unit output given bit availability constraints. Jensen signaling confidence on AI share wins vs. ASICs per Mizuho buyside checks. Separately, SpaceX seeking ~$30B IG debt to finance NVIDIA chip purchases; NVDA announced $500B third-party AI compute financing pool.

bullets.title: AVGO: Arranging $50B+ financing for custom OpenAI chips; buyside sentiment weakest in northeast
bullets.body: Broadcom is arranging $50B+ in financing (Apollo and Blackstone as potential lenders) for custom chips destined for OpenAI. Despite the capex tailwind, Mizuho notes buyside AVGO sentiment was worst in the northeast; positioning could support upside if Mediatek V9 TPU delays are confirmed. Citi TMT consensus has AVGO shorts on competition as a crowded tactical trade.

bullets.title: ORCL: GPU financing discussions with Apollo/Goldman; key catalyst is FY28 cash flow inflection
bullets.body: Oracle is in discussions with Apollo and Goldman Sachs for a large GPU purchase financing arrangement. Mizuho buyside checks see ORCL as a potential 2H27 rebounder with the key catalyst being cash flow inflection in FY28 as current cash burn reverses.

bullets.title: META: Muse #1 US App Store 22 days running; launched ahead of schedule due to Instinct competitive threat
bullets.body: Meta's Muse has been the #1 US App Store app for 22 consecutive days; Citi notes META delayed Muse release over privacy concerns but pulled forward the launch due to Instinct competitive pressure. META also banned ByteDance ads. Muse is driving the OTA/marketplace selloff and the broader 'agent layer' debate across consumer internet.

bullets.title: DELL/MU/AMD/INTC: PC shipments -20% y/y in 3Q26; semiconductor exposure flagged as headwind
bullets.body: IDC reports 3Q26 PC shipments fell 20.1% y/y to 62.7M units (vs -3.8% in 2Q), driven by 1H pull-in exhaustion and elevated inventory. Dell down 25%, HP down 30.9%, Apple down 11.3% in units. KeyBanc September notebook ODM data confirms -18% y/y at 13.8M units, below their 15.3M estimate. PC-exposed semis (AMD, INTC, MU, NVDA) flagged as negatively impacted.

bullets.title: DLR/EQIX: Data center supply/demand imbalance bullish; 65 GW under construction vs. accelerating demand
bullets.body: Jefferies data center pipeline model forecasts 12.9 GW new NA capacity in 2026, 18 GW in 2027, and 26 GW in 2028 — with 33%+ growth rates through 2028. ~65 GW is under construction (~140% of installed base) but labor/permitting remain gating factors (electrician employment up only 15% in 5 years vs. 6x capacity delivery expected). DLR/EQIX own ~3 GW in markets with the most acute imbalances; hyperscalers increasingly leasing vs. self-building.

bullets.title: WULF/HUT: MS raises powered-shell capex yield to 19%; raises PTs for both names
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Stephen Byrd updated his power-shell framework, raising capex yield assumptions from 15% to 19% to offset higher cost of capital; terminal cap rate moves to 6.7% (from 5%) and debt coupons to 7% for hyperscaler, 10% for neocloud deals. Byrd raises price targets for HUT and WULF (also APLD); lowers MARA, RIOT.

bullets.title: TSLA: Cybercab registrations doubled two weeks in a row
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley TMT note flags that Tesla Cybercab registrations have doubled for two consecutive weeks, the most recent positive datapoint ahead of launch. No price target action cited in this note.

bullets.title: SPOT: Citi reiterates Buy with $620 PT; Q3 in-line, Q4 gross margin slightly below Street
bullets.body: Citi maintains Buy on Spotify with $620 PT (27x 2027E FCF). Q3 operating income estimate is €653M vs. Street at €675M. Q4 gross margin expected at 33.3% vs. Street's 33.9% due to international expansion costs. Wolfe separately notes gross margin forecasts need to come down further (33.6% vs. 33.9% consensus) and sees audiobooks as a 2027 upside catalyst.

bullets.title: NYT: Morgan Stanley cuts PT to $75 from $90; video investment headwinds pressure near-term
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley maintained Equal-Weight on NYT but cut PT from $90 to $75, implying ~15x forward EBITDA (vs. prior 19x). Shares have underperformed S&P by ~20pts YTD. Video investment is accelerating opex growth to +8.5% YoY in 2026 from the historical ~4-5%, compressing EBITDA/EPS by 2-4%. Q3 digital net adds expected to moderate to ~200k; engagement softness may reflect AI search traffic headwinds.

bullets.title: CRWD: Vendor consolidation driving share gains; pricing pressure on QLYS/TENB/RPD
bullets.body: Two VAR checks (GuidePoint via DA Davidson; separate security survey) confirm CRWD gaining share as customers consolidate cybersecurity budgets that remain flat YoY. CRWD actively putting pricing pressure on vulnerability management incumbents QLYS, TENB, and RPD. PANW struck the most confident tone at Citi's software bus tour; NET flagged as positive read from Vercel commentary.

bullets.title: GOOGL: 120+ lawmakers raise privacy concerns over planned Spirit Airlines data acquisition
bullets.body: Alphabet's plan to acquire Spirit Airlines passenger/employee data to train AI models has prompted objections from more than 120 US lawmakers focused on employee data protection. No financial impact quantified yet, but adds to GOOGL's regulatory overhang.

bullets.title: TSM: Taiwan exports +61% y/y in September; TSMC revenues near NT$500B, fresh USD records
bullets.body: Taiwan September exports jumped 61% y/y and 8% m/m, with ICT products surging 23% m/m to an all-time high of $41B. TSMC revenues rose 0.7% m/m (sa) to nearly NT$500B, setting fresh USD records. Taiwan Manufacturing PMI jumped 2pts to 56.7 in September — a series with ~70% correlation to US ISM (1-month lead).

bullets.title: CHTR: Down 33% as creditor CoBank sues to block Mega Broadband acquisition, cites insolvency
bullets.body: CoBank filed a lawsuit and is seeking a restraining order to block Charter's acquisition of the remaining 55% of Mega Broadband (Vyve) for $475-495M, alleging the deal overvalues Mega Broadband and that CHTR is insolvent. CHTR was reportedly in advanced talks on a new $1.25B financing package as of yesterday; Mega generates ~$310M annual revenue with ~210k customers.

bullets.title: TEAM/ACN/MRVL: Upcoming investor days; MRVL analyst day coverage flagged by Wolfe
bullets.body: Applied Materials (AMAT) and Atlassian (TEAM) hosting investor days Tuesday; Accenture (ACN) hosting Wednesday per JPM credit note. Wolfe Research flagging MRVL analyst day as a key near-term event in its semiconductor webcast today.
